claimResults.fixIsRootCause: Largely yes, with caveats. The fix addresses the cause (low space is signalled too late when old space cannot grow, so the scavenger runs out first). It is a design heuristic, not a hard guarantee: the threshold of 2 x newSpaceCapacity does not prove that one scavenge cannot tenure more. A single scavenge can in principle tenure up to the whole of new space, so one new space is enough for it, and the second new space is for the unwind. Not a workaround (no skip, no retry). Side change: the old loop returned true early once growHeadroom was reached; the new loop condition uses max(growHeadroom, lowMark), which is equivalent when growth succeeds. I did not run it.

verified.whyNotTestBug: The defects are in non-test classes of package Collections-Atomic: AtomicSharedQueue>>next / WaitfreeQueue>>nextIfNone:. (Q1) a reader that finds the queue locked by another reader waits again and uses up the signal for its item, and the reader with the lock gives no signal, so an item stays in the queue. (Q2) a reader that sends signalNoMoreItems (availSema consumeAllSignals) can reset the signal of an item that a writer put in meanwhile and then waits with a non-empty queue. (Q3) a reader terminated inside nextIfNone: leaves the queue locked forever (dummy makeCircular never undone), while flush: and nextOrNilSuchThat: already protect with ifCurtailed:. The fix changes those three methods; the tests are new and only demonstrate them.

verified.userVisibleImpact: On macOS, setting a window title or starting the SDL backend over-releases a CFString. If the thread's autorelease pool drains (a VM that runs the interpreter on a secondary thread of a GUI app, as ours does, drains at thread exit), the process crashes with '-[CFString release]: message sent to deallocated instance'. On the stock command-line Cog VM no pool is drained, so the defect is latent. Any macOS embedder that wraps the interpreter in a pool also hits the crash.

verified.testForPR: No automated test is feasible: needs macOS with Cocoa and an autorelease pool.
